title: Load-balanced web tier
purpose: Explain DNS resolution separately from HTTP requests and distribution to two private web servers.
alt: DNS 조회 후 공인 주소의 로드밸런서를 거쳐 사설 웹 서버에 요청하는 흐름
requiredChecks: DNS lookup and public endpoint response are separate from the HTTP path; DNS does not forward HTTP.
Client HTTP enters public Load balancer, which distributes to two Web servers within Private network.
Private connections are clearly labeled; server pair is parallel, not chained.
Labels and arrow directions readable; no guarantee that a single balancer removes all failure points.
prompt: Create a NEW original English technical educational raster diagram, white background, large navy sans-serif labels, flat blue/teal cards, clear separated orthogonal arrows and generous gutters. No logos, decorative imagery, copied textbook composition, numeric benchmarks or absolute availability promises. TITLE "Load-balanced web tier". Left-to-right request row: "Client"→"Load balancer"→parallel "Web server A" and "Web server B". Loadbalancer subtitle "Public endpoint"; both webservers enclosed in "Private network" boundary. Connections from balancer toward each server labelled "Private IP". Above Client a separate "DNS resolver" card with Client→DNS arrow "1. DNS lookup" and a separate DNS→Client arrow "2. Public endpoint". Main Client→Loadbalancer arrow labelled "3. HTTP request". No DNS→loadbalancer connector, no HTTP throughDNS. Footer "Distribute requests across healthy web servers". Give two DNS arrows distinct tracks and labels; align everything to avoid intersections.
